manual.sawmill.line2: The sawmill is a machine assembly which cuts wooden logs into neatly stacked planks.{0}
manual.sawmill.line3: The machine operates in two stages: first, the log is stripped, then the stripped law is cut apart using a {0}sawblade{1}.{2}
manual.sawmill.line4: {0}Both steps of the process create §2sawdust§r, which is collected and output through the port at the front of the machine.{1}
manual.sawmill.line5: That sawdust can later be processed into paper or other useful materials, such as {0}Fiberboard{1}.{2}
manual.sawmill.line6: The machine is built as shown on the first page and formed by using an §2Engineer's Hammer§r on the central sheetmetal block.{0}
manual.sawmill.line7: Applying a redstone signal to the control panel at the front will stop the machine, this behavior can be inverted by the §2Engineer's Screwdriver§r.{0}
manual.sawmill.line8: To be ready for processing, you will need to craft a {0}sawblade{1} and insert it into the slot on the back by right-clicking. Sneak and right-click to take the sawblade out again.{2}
manual.sawmill.line9: Trying to remove the sawblade while in operation will cause injury. To ensure the machine is not in operation, disable the machine with redstone while the machine is empty.{0}
manual.sawmill.line10: Running logs through the machine without a sawblade will create §2stripped logs§r that will not be cut apart. This process is much quicker than stripping them manually.{0}
manual.sawmill.line11: The sawblade will be damaged while it's in use and may need to be replaced after a while.
